title: NA session: lawmakers press need to strengthen social harmony - The Rising Nepal
description: NA session: lawmakers press need to strengthen social harmony  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 3: Members in the National Assembly (NA) have underlined the need of keeping social harmony intact in the present adverse situation.

Speaking in the 'special hour' of a meeting of the National Assembly (NA) today, they urged the government to address farmers' concerns, ensure job opportunities for youths within the country, maintain mutual harmony and implement effective measures against human trafficking.

Samjhana Devkota proposed the collaboration between the federal and local governments to ease the communal tense in Sunsari of Koshi Province and in the Madhesh Province. She demanded the government provide jobs to youths and be proactive to consolidate the social harmony.

Rajendra Laxmi Gaire expressed concerns over new forms evolving in human traffic, adding that effective strategies are vital for controlling them.

Lack of job opportunities at home has compelled many citizens including women, to seek foreign employment, sometimes making them vulnerable to human trafficking racket, she said, urging the government to take special measures address the situation.

She also utilised the time to call on the government to prioritise the long-standing issue of landless people and address them swiftly.

Lawmakers also during the special hour called on the government to work in deference to the people's trust and aspirations.

They said that since people look to the government for solutions to all their problems, officials should work according to that.

Those lawmakers expressing their views in this line include Kiran Babu Shrestha of the Nepali Congress, Rukmini Koirala of the CPN (UML) and Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari of the Nepali Communist Party (NCP).

Nepali Congress' Dharmendra Paswan emphasized that everyone’s attention should be focused on achieving peace and prosperity in the country through dialogue, reconciliation, and coordination.

NCP's Bhuwan Bahadur Sunuwar drew the government's attention to the demands of meter usurious lending victims who are still at Maitighar Mandala pressing for their demands. UML MP Rekha Kumari Jha highlighted to the government the need to control smuggling and criminal activities taking advantage of the Nepal-India open border.

Meantime, the upper house members have drawn the government's attention to various contemporary pressing issues including the price rise of daily commodities, shortage of cooking gas, ongoing discriminations on Dalit community, border issues and issues concerning public health.

Airing views in a zero hour of the National Assembly (NA) meeting today, Krishna Bahadur Rokaya said the citizens have been hit by the market inflation, while Bishnu Kumari Sapkota urged the government to promptly undertake measures to control the price hike.

Shree Krishna Prasad Adhikari expressed his concern over the shortage of cooking gas, inflation and consequences on public health due to pesticide- contaminated foodstuffs.

Padam Bahadur Pariyar said the caste-based discrimination against Dalits have not ended, while Pooja Chaudhary drew the government's attention to the urgency to address the border issues in Susta of Nawalparasi West through diplomatic dealings.

Renu Chand demanded a fair investigation into the case relating to the death of Pooja Dhanuk of Sudurpaschim.(RSS)

title: Former Finance Minister Khanal calls for revival programme to protect MSMEs - The Rising Nepal
description: Former Finance Minister Khanal calls for revival programme to protect MSMEs  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 3: Former Finance Minister Rameshore Khanal has said that extensive improvements in insurance, loans, and policy structures are necessary for the revival of micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs) that were hit hard after COVID-19.

Addressing to the policy discussion programme organized here today by the Society of Economic Journalists Nepal (SEJON), Nepal Insurance Authority, and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to release the study report ‘Risk Management in Nepal’s MSMEs’, former Finance Minister Khanal said that policy reforms are needed to protect and promote MSMEs facing economic crises.

He pointed out that although MSMEs play an important role in the economy, the sector has become weak due to a lack of risk management and financial access.

The former finance minister suggested introducing innovative measures in the agriculture insurance programme, such as the government initially covering 100 per cent of the premium for poor farmers and having them pay their share only after receiving compensation, noting that even though the government provides up to 75 per cent premium subsidy, farmers have not been able to fully benefit from it.

"According to the report that was made public on the occasion, only 10 per cent of the nearly 900 thousand MSMEs in Nepal have access to insurance, while the remaining 90 per cent are unprotected against any risks," he said, adding, "Even though sectors like tourism and construction are gradually recovering after COVID-19, MSMEs are still in crisis, and this situation has contributed to an increase in bad loans and non-banking assets in banks and financial institutions."

On the occasion, Kalpana Shrestha, Joint Secretary of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, highlighted the need to expand insurance access by integrating the various programmes run by the government to promote micro, small, and medium enterprises.

She mentioned that since nearly 50 per cent of the approximately 923 thousand MSMEs in Nepal are in the informal sector and thus outside the scope of insurance, overall insurance coverage is limited to about 10 per cent. Considering this, the government is running programmes like startup loans, MEDPA programmes, production-based incentives, and the National Enterprise Facility to promote entrepreneurship.

UNDP Nepal's resident representative Kyoko Yokosuka said that although micro, small, and medium enterprises are the backbone of Nepal's economy, they are the most affected by increasing climate and economic risks.

She mentioned that UNDP, through the 'Insurance and Risk Finance Facility,' is working with 39 countries including Nepal to strengthen financial protection against climate and disaster risks, and expressed a continued commitment to helping expand affordable and appropriate insurance access for MSMEs in Nepal.

Sushildev Subedi, Executive Director of the Nepal Insurance Authority, said that it is necessary to make the insurance system more inclusive, modern, and effective to protect micro, small, and medium enterprises from various risks.

He also expressed the view that MSMEs are the most affected by risks like natural disasters, climate change, financial crises, cyber risks, and health emergencies, so effective risk management is indispensable.(RSS)

हुनी ई भी विचार व्यक्त करलकै कि एमएसएमई प्राकृतिक आपदा, जलवायु परिवर्तन, वित्तीय संकट, साइबर जोखिम, आरू स्वास्थ्य आपातकाल जैसनऽ जोखिम स॑ सबसें जादा प्रभावित छै, ई लेली प्रभावी जोखिम प्रबंधन अनिवार्य छै ।(आरएसएस)

publisher.title: Ratopati
full_article: Kathmandu. The sister organization of the Nepali Congress, Nepal Tarun Dal, has directed its cadres not to participate in any unauthorized activities that go against the party's policies, rules, and procedures. Party Central President Manish Koirala issued a press release on Monday, directing against violating institutional discipline and warning of initiating disciplinary action. 'All are hereby cautioned not to engage in or cause to be engaged in any unauthorized act in the name of the Dal by individuals who have deviated from the ideology, programs, and plans specified by the Dal, with the intention of creating confusion,' President Koirala wrote in the press release. The press release has urged not to participate in such programs, pointing to recent instances where some individuals or interest groups have been organizing separate gatherings or assemblies in the name of Tarun Dal. Stating that institutional discipline, continuity, and commitment are the main ornaments of Tarun Dal, President Koirala said that Tarun Dal is firm in the guidance of BP Koirala and democratic ideals.

title: Foreign Minister Khanal, visiting ex-PM from Mongolia meet, discuss potential cooperation in multiple areas - The Rising Nepal
description: Foreign Minister Khanal, visiting ex-PM from Mongolia meet, discuss potential cooperation in multiple areas  The Rising Nepal
publisher.title: The Rising Nepal
full_article:
Kathmandu, Aug 3: Visiting former Prime Minister of Mongolia, Gombojavyn Zandanshatar, today paid a courtesy call on Minister for Foreign Affairs, Shisir Khanal.

In the meeting held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the two discussed Nepal-Mongolia bilateral relations, geopolitical similarities, and the potential cooperation in the areas of development, trade, partnership and Buddhist norms and values.

On the occasion, the Minister said Nepal and Mongolia share similarities in terms of geopolitics, adding that Nepal is eager to learn from Mongolia's experiences across various areas.

He said Nepal is interested in expanding the bilateral cooperation in the areas of development, trade, partnership and Buddhist norms and values.

As he said, Nepal and Mongolia can raise their voices collectively for the rights and interests of land-locked countries.

He applauded Mongolia for maintaining balanced relations with its neighboring countries and demonstrating effective partnership management.

During the meeting, the two also explored possible ways to further strengthen bilateral and diplomatic relations between Nepal and Mongolia.

Minister Khanal said that the government of Nepal is keen to further strengthening relations with Mongolia as a spiritual partner. He clarified that Nepal is committed to advancing cooperation between the two countries across various areas.

In response, the Mongolia's former Prime Minister talked about the geographical similarities between the two countries, pressing the need for small countries like Nepal and Mongolia to move ahead in unison in the changing global system.

He said that Nepal and Mongolia share common Buddhist values and culture, and that both countries are spiritual neighbors. He added that Mongolia is keen to cooperate with Nepal in the areas of Buddhist values, culture and the development of chess in Nepal.(RSS)

हुनी मंगोलिया क॑ अपनऽ पड़ोसी देशऽ के साथ संतुलित संबंध बनाबै आरू प्रभावी साझेदारी प्रबंधन के प्रदर्शन करै लेली तारीफ करलकै ।

ओ कहलनि जे नेपाल आ मंगोलिया मे बौद्ध मूल्य आ संस्कृति साझा अछि, आ दुनू देश आध्यात्मिक पड़ोसी अछि । ओ इहो कहलनि जे, नेपाल मे बौद्ध मूल्य, संस्कृति आ शतरंज के विकास के क्षेत्र मे मंगोलिया नेपाल के संग सहयोग करय लेल उत्सुक अछि।(RSS)

title: Nepal's July foreign tourist arrivals edge up - The Star
description: Nepal's July foreign tourist arrivals edge up  The Star
publisher.title: The Star
full_article:
KATHMANDU: Foreign tourist arrivals to Nepal increased by 2.3 percent in July compared with the same month last year, driven mainly by a sharp rise in visitors from China and the United States, according to Nepal Tourism Board.

The board said in its monthly report released on Monday that Nepal welcomed 71,775 international traveler visits in July, up from 70,193 arrivals recorded during the same month in 2025.

Even as Indian tourists continued to account for the largest share of foreign visitors, with 23,490 arrivals during the month, the number declined compared to the same period last year, according to the board. - Xinhua

बोर्ड सोमदिन जारी अपन मासिक रिपोर्ट मे कहलक अछि जे नेपाल मे जुलाई मे 71,775 अंतरराष्ट्रीय यात्रीक यात्राक स्वागत भेल अछि, जखन कि 2025 मे एहि मास मे 70,193 आगमन दर्ज भेल अछि।
